title: John Ross House (Rossville, Georgia)
axis: Local X follows the 50-foot long log wall. Negative Z faces the visitor approach and pond.
source: Current OpenStreetMap building rectangle identified by its physical footprint, position and the National Park Service property record.

features.role: Current standing building outline including the porches

identityStatus: The mapped rectangle is about 16.01 m by 10.49 m and aligns with the standing house identified by the National Park Service. The main log walls are 50 by 16 feet, with 23, 11 and 16-foot subdivisions. The difference in mapped depth accommodates the two porches.

terrainContact.basis: Original USGS near the center of the visitor approach on the north side.

notes: Native National Trails Office photographs show exterior log courses with light chinking, visible rafter tails, two exterior stone chimneys, closed rustic shutters and two low porch roofs. The landmark nomination confirms the wall dimensions and breezeway.
